# Plan: User Dashboard Page

## Context
We're shipping a new user dashboard at `/dashboard` showing recent activity,
notifications panel, and quick-action buttons. Users land here after login.

## UI Scope
- New React page component `UserDashboard.tsx` at `src/pages/`
- Three new sub-components: `ActivityFeed`, `NotificationsPanel`, `QuickActions`
- Tailwind CSS for layout, mobile-first responsive (breakpoints: sm/md/lg)
- Empty state, loading skeleton, error state for each panel
- Hover states + focus-visible outlines on every interactive element
- Modal dialog for "Mark all as read" on notifications panel
- Toast notification system for action feedback

## Backend
- New REST endpoint `GET /api/dashboard` returns `{ activity, notifications, quickActions }`
- Backed by existing PostgreSQL tables; no schema changes

## Out of scope
- Dark mode (separate plan)
- Personalization / customization (separate plan)

## Existing product and application contracts

This is the existing single-role member workspace, not a new product or a new
onboarding flow. Members currently visit three separate pages after login to
resume work, check alerts, and inspect recent changes. In the team's last task
walkthrough, finding the next item took a median 75 seconds. The dashboard's
success measure is login-to-first-completed-task time, targeting 45 seconds,
with completed-task rate and permission-error rate as guardrails. Existing
analytics records login, action start, action completion, and permission errors;
the new page still needs its own exposure and interaction instrumentation.

Activity is the immutable audit history of workspace changes. Notifications are
member-specific alerts with persistent read state; acknowledging an alert does
not alter audit history. The existing action registry supplies three actions
(create an item, resume assigned work, invite a member), with stable IDs, labels,
route targets, and server-side eligibility predicates. These are links into
existing workflows; action ranking and a new configuration service do not exist.

The application already uses cookie sessions and workspace membership middleware.
Its request context supplies the authenticated member and workspace IDs. Existing
repository methods apply both IDs where appropriate; callers do not accept a
workspace ID from query parameters. Mutations already require CSRF tokens. The
new dashboard endpoint must compose these methods and follow the same boundaries;
its handler, authorization integration, and failure paths have not been written.

Existing list methods return the latest 20 records plus a cursor and have indexed
workspace/member and created-at access paths. The existing full activity and
notification pages own older-page navigation. The member-scoped bulk-read API is
idempotent and marks only notifications at or before the supplied snapshot time,
so later arrivals remain unread. Existing HTTP clients expose typed unauthenticated,
forbidden, validation, retryable-service, and network errors. Each dashboard panel
still needs to map these results to its loading, empty, error, retry, and success
states; the aggregate endpoint's response composition and partial-failure behavior
remain new implementation work. No schema migration or new mutation API is needed.

The app already has Tailwind spacing/color/type tokens, a responsive page shell,
buttons, links, and a dialog primitive with focus trapping, Escape dismissal, and
focus return. These primitives do not implement any dashboard panel, confirmation
flow, or toast system. The new modal and toast feedback must also work with keyboard
and screen readers; existing accessibility policy requires named controls, a live
region for nonblocking feedback, sufficient contrast, and reduced-motion support.
The dashboard still needs its own layout, content hierarchy, mobile behavior, and
state-specific copy at sm/md/lg breakpoints.

Vitest, React Testing Library, and Playwright already run in CI. Existing fixtures
cover authenticated members, another workspace, empty lists, and service failures;
there are no dashboard-specific tests yet. Existing staging feature flags and
request/error metrics support a member-cohort rollout and rollback to the current
landing page. The dashboard's rollout criteria, endpoint performance checks,
interaction tests, and accessibility verification must be specified and added.

All dashboard screen, panel, aggregate-endpoint, modal, and toast work listed above
is new. The existing contracts describe dependencies to reuse, not completed work
or prior approval of an implementation approach.

<!-- autoplan-accepted:ceo -->
- Dashboard endpoint returns panel-level partial failure: `{error: true, message: string}` per failing panel; successful panels always returned. Frontend panels independently handle error state.
- Aggregate endpoint uses parallel fetches (Promise.all or backend equivalent) — sequential execution prohibited.
- Rate limiting applied to GET /api/dashboard at API gateway layer (same tier as existing endpoints).
- XSS: all user-generated content (notification messages, activity text) rendered as text nodes, never innerHTML. React JSX default is sufficient if props are string-typed; no dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Double-click protection: confirm button disabled on modal submit; re-enabled on error response.
- Network error on mark-all-read mutation: error toast shown, modal stays open for retry.
- Quick action eligibility server-side re-check: 403 → toast "Action no longer available."
- Panel retry: re-fetches GET /api/dashboard; failed panel re-renders from new response.
- DashboardPanel shared wrapper component: handles loading/empty/error/retry state machine. Each panel specializes only success content.
- All 12 test scenarios in Section 6 required before rollout.
- 20% holdout group in feature flag rollout. Go/no-go: login-to-first-task mean ≤ 45s vs. holdout, permission-error delta ≤ +2%, p95 < 200ms.
- p95 target: GET /api/dashboard < 200ms. Alert at > 500ms p95.
- Dashboard instrumentation: metrics and structured logs as specified in Section 8.
- Rollout criteria: Phase 1 (5% internal), Phase 2 (20% + 20% holdout), Phase 3 (full). Rollback: feature flag flip on error rate > 5%/5m.
- Toast system: singleton store. API: `toast.show({message, type, duration?})`. Max 3 concurrent. Bottom-right. `aria-live="polite"`.
- Panel order: QuickActions (top), NotificationsPanel (middle), ActivityFeed (bottom). Mobile: vertical stack. md/lg: 2-column (QA+NP left, AF right).
- State copy: Activity empty: "No recent workspace activity." Notif empty: "You're all caught up." Error: panel-specific "Could not load X — Retry."
- Accessibility gate: required before phase-1 rollout. axe scan zero violations + keyboard walkthrough + VoiceOver/NVDA spot-check.

### Step 0A: Premise Challenge

Three premises examined:

**Premise 1 (accepted):** Three-page flow causes friction; aggregation reduces it.
75s median → 45s target is plausible. The existing analytics baseline already exists. Accepted (P6 — bias toward action; user has context we lack).

**Premise 2 (accepted):** Existing PostgreSQL tables require no schema changes.
Plan says endpoint composes existing repo methods. Plausible given read-only aggregation. Accepted.

**Premise 3 (CRITICAL GAP — auto-fixed):** Aggregate endpoint partial-failure behavior is undefined.
If the activity fetch fails but notifications succeed, the plan does not specify whether the endpoint returns 500 or partial data. This is implementation-blocking. Auto-fixed: endpoint returns panel-level isolation — partial data with failed panels returning `{error: true}` (Decision #2).

**Premise 4 (accepted as-is):** Action registry (create item, resume assigned work, invite member) is the correct action set.
No usage frequency data provided. User has more context. Accepted, noted in NOT IN SCOPE for future validation.

**CEO Subagent challenge on premises (HIGH):** The subagent identified that Premise 1 may be wrong — the friction could be cognitive load, not navigation cost. If users take 75s because they are evaluating what to do next (not because they are navigating), a dashboard does not reduce that. This is surfaced as Taste Decision T1 for Final Gate.

## CEO Review Sections

### Section 1: Architecture Review

**System architecture:**

```
Browser                     API Layer                      DB / Registry
──────────                  ─────────                      ─────────────
GET /dashboard  ──────────► DashboardPage
                             ├─ DashboardPanel (shared wrapper)
                             │   ├─ ActivityFeed
                             │   ├─ NotificationsPanel
                             │   └─ QuickActions
                             │
                             ▼
                            GET /api/dashboard  ─────────► Promise.all([
                             │                               activityRepo.list(member, ws),
                             │                               notifRepo.list(member, ws),
                             │                               actionRegistry.eligible(member)
                             │                             ])
                             │                             ▼
                             │                     Panel-level isolation:
                             │                     {activity: data|{error:true},
                             │                      notifications: data|{error:true},
                             │                      quickActions: data|{error:true}}
                             │
                            Toast singleton ◄──────── "Mark all read" modal
                                                       CSRF token + snapshot time
                                                       PATCH /api/notifications/read-all
```

**Data flow (happy path):**
```
User → /dashboard → GET /api/dashboard → Promise.all(3 queries) → 200 {activity, notifications, quickActions}
→ Dashboard renders 3 panels in success state
```

**Data flow (partial failure):**
```
activityRepo fails (TimeoutError) → activity: {error:true}
notifRepo succeeds → notifications: data
actionRegistry succeeds → quickActions: data
Endpoint returns 200 with mixed payload → frontend: ActivityFeed shows error UI, others show success
```

**Finding S1-1: Partial failure contract undefined** → Auto-fixed (Decision #2): endpoint returns panel-level isolation; failed panels return `{error: true, message: string}`.

**Finding S1-2: Sequential vs parallel fetches unspecified** → Auto-fixed (Decision #3): `Promise.all` (or backend equivalent) for all three sub-calls. Sequential would triple p99 latency.

**Security architecture:**
- Auth: cookie session + workspace membership middleware. No new query params for member/workspace IDs. ✓
- CSRF: mark-all-read mutation uses existing CSRF tokens. ✓
- No new secrets. ✓
- No new dependencies. ✓

**Rollback posture:** Feature flag flip = immediate rollback. No DB migration to reverse. ✓

**Finding S1-3: Rate limiting on aggregate endpoint** → Auto-fixed (Decision #4): rate limit at API gateway layer matching existing endpoint limits. Dashboard is called per page load; without rate limiting, a rapid refresher makes 3 parallel DB queries per call.

### Section 2: Error & Rescue Map

```
METHOD/CODEPATH               | WHAT CAN GO WRONG              | EXCEPTION CLASS
------------------------------|--------------------------------|-------------------
GET /api/dashboard handler    | DB connection failure          | ConnectionError
                              | Individual repo timeout        | TimeoutError
                              | Auth session expired           | UnauthenticatedError
                              | Workspace access revoked       | ForbiddenError
PATCH notifications/read-all  | CSRF token expired             | CSRFError
                              | Network failure                | NetworkError
                              | Auth expired mid-modal         | UnauthenticatedError
Frontend panel fetch          | Typed HTTP 4xx/5xx             | typed HTTPError

EXCEPTION CLASS         | RESCUED? | RESCUE ACTION                        | USER SEES
------------------------|----------|--------------------------------------|-------------------
ConnectionError         | Y        | Return panel {error:true}             | Panel error UI + retry
TimeoutError            | Y        | Return panel {error:true}             | Panel error UI + retry
UnauthenticatedError    | Y        | 401 → frontend redirects to login    | Login page
ForbiddenError          | Y        | 403 → panel error or page redirect   | Access denied UI
CSRFError               | Y        | 403 → toast "Session expired, refresh"| Error toast
NetworkError            | Y        | Error toast, modal stays open        | "Request failed, try again"
typed HTTPError         | Y        | Per-type: 4xx→panel error, 5xx→retry | Panel error UI
```

**Finding S2-1 (auto-fixed, Decision #5):** Add this error rescue table to the implementation plan. Catch-all error handling explicitly prohibited; each exception class named.

### Section 3: Security & Threat Model

```
THREAT                               | LIKELIHOOD | IMPACT | MITIGATED?
-------------------------------------|-----------|--------|------------
IDOR via dashboard endpoint          | Low        | High   | YES — member+ws from session, not params
Session fixation / auth bypass       | Low        | High   | YES — existing cookie+middleware
CSRF on mark-all-read mutation       | Low        | Med    | YES — existing CSRF token system
Rate limiting on aggregate endpoint  | Med        | Med    | ADDED (Decision #4)
XSS via notification/activity content| Med        | High   | Depends on rendering (sanitize)
```

**Finding S3-1: XSS in notification/activity content** — The plan doesn't specify that notification messages and activity text are rendered as text, not innerHTML. If any field is rendered raw, XSS is possible.
→ Auto-decide (Decision #6): Add to plan: "All user-generated content (notification messages, activity descriptions) rendered as text nodes, never innerHTML. React's default JSX rendering satisfies this if props are string-typed."

No other critical security findings. Auth boundaries are correctly specified.

### Section 4: Data Flow & Interaction Edge Cases

**Data flows diagrammed in Section 1.** Shadow paths:
- Nil activity/notification input → empty state panels ✓ (plan specifies empty states)
- Network failure during load → error state panels ✓ (plan specifies error states)
- Concurrent new notification during dashboard session → not addressed (static snapshot on page load, no real-time updates — acceptable given no SSE/polling in scope)

**Interaction edge cases:**

```
INTERACTION               | EDGE CASE                      | STATUS    | FIX
--------------------------|--------------------------------|-----------|----------------------------------------
Modal confirm             | Double-click submit            | GAP       | Disable button on submit, re-enable on error
Modal confirm             | Network error during mutation  | GAP       | Error toast, modal stays open for retry
Quick action click        | Eligibility changes post-load  | GAP       | Server-side eligibility re-check; 403 → toast
Dashboard load            | Session expires between panels | Handled   | UnauthenticatedError → redirect to login
Mark-all-read             | New notif arrives during open  | Handled   | Snapshot time prevents marking future notifs
Panel retry button        | User clicks retry on error     | GAP       | Retry re-fetches GET /api/dashboard, panel re-renders
Activity/notif list       | Zero results                   | Handled   | Empty states specified
```

**Finding S4-1 (auto-fixed, Decision #7):** Double-click protection — disable confirm button on submit.
**Finding S4-2 (auto-fixed, Decision #8):** Network error during mutation — error toast + modal stays open.
**Finding S4-3 (auto-fixed, Decision #9):** Quick action eligibility re-check — server-side 403 → toast "Action no longer available."
**Finding S4-4 (auto-fixed, Decision #10):** Panel retry — re-fetches aggregate endpoint, failed panel re-renders.

### Section 5: Code Quality Review

**DRY finding:** Three panels each need loading/empty/error/retry state machines. Implementing this 3× in each sub-component is a DRY violation.

**Finding S5-1 (auto-fixed, Decision #11):** Extract `DashboardPanel` shared wrapper component that handles loading/empty/error/retry. Each panel (ActivityFeed, NotificationsPanel, QuickActions) specializes only its success content. Single state machine implementation, 3 specialized consumers.

Code organization: `UserDashboard.tsx` in `src/pages/` ✓. Sub-components in `src/components/dashboard/` (follow existing pattern). Endpoint in existing API route structure ✓.

Naming: `ActivityFeed`, `NotificationsPanel`, `QuickActions`, `DashboardPanel` — clear, domain-language names. ✓

No over-engineering concerns. No complexity violations (each component has a simple, well-defined role).

### Section 6: Test Review

**New UX flows:**
1. Dashboard loads → all 3 panels populated (success state)
2. Dashboard loads → empty states per panel
3. Dashboard loads → 1+ panel in error state (partial failure)
4. Mark all as read → happy path (modal → confirm → toast → panel refresh)
5. Mark all as read → cancel path (modal → cancel → no change)
6. Mark all as read → error path (mutation fails → error toast → modal stays)
7. Quick action click → navigates to correct destination
8. Panel retry → re-fetches → panel recovers to success
9. Keyboard navigation through all interactive elements
10. Mobile rendering at sm/md/lg breakpoints

**New data flows:**
1. `GET /api/dashboard` → parallel fetch → aggregate response (all success)
2. `GET /api/dashboard` → partial failure → mixed response
3. `PATCH /api/notifications/read-all` → success
4. `PATCH /api/notifications/read-all` → failure

**Test coverage map:**

```
FLOW / CODEPATH                        | TEST TYPE         | EXISTS?
---------------------------------------|-------------------|--------
Dashboard page render (all success)    | RTL component     | No → T-S6-1
Dashboard page render (empty panels)   | RTL component     | No → T-S6-2
Dashboard page render (partial failure)| RTL component     | No → T-S6-3
Aggregate endpoint (all success)       | Vitest unit       | No → T-S6-4
Aggregate endpoint (partial failure)   | Vitest unit       | No → T-S6-5
Mark all read (success)                | RTL + Playwright  | No → T-S6-6
Mark all read (failure)                | RTL               | No → T-S6-7
Quick action click                     | RTL               | No → T-S6-8
Keyboard nav (full flow)               | Playwright        | No → T-S6-9
Accessibility (axe scan)               | Playwright/axe    | No → T-S6-10
Mobile responsive (sm/md/lg)           | Playwright        | No → T-S6-11
Holdout group rollout metrics          | Manual / feature flag | No → T-S6-12
```

**Finding S6-1 (auto-fixed, Decision #12):** All test specs listed above added to implementation plan. Tests are non-negotiable (P1).

**Finding S6-2 (auto-fixed, Decision #13):** Feature flag holdout group — 20% holdout for controlled A/B measurement of login-to-first-completed-task. Without a holdout, the 45s target cannot be verified.

### Section 7: Performance Review

**Query analysis:**
- 2 indexed DB queries per page load (activity + notifications), parallel
- Action registry: in-memory, no DB hit
- Total: 2 parallel indexed queries → estimated p95 < 100ms under normal load

N+1: No association traversal. Flat list queries only. ✓
Memory: 20 records × 2 panels = 40 rows in memory. Trivial. ✓

**Finding S7-1 (auto-fixed, Decision #14):** Add p95 latency target to plan: `GET /api/dashboard` target p95 < 200ms. Alert threshold: p95 > 500ms. Monitor via existing request metrics.

Caching: Quick actions are static — can be cached in memory (trivially). Activity and notifications are user-specific and frequently updated — do not cache. No caching added (P3 pragmatic — caching adds complexity for minimal gain on 2 fast indexed queries).

### Section 8: Observability & Debuggability Review

**Required instrumentation (auto-decided — Decision #15):**

```
Metric/log                                        | Type
--------------------------------------------------|------
dashboard.page.loaded                             | Counter (exposure)
dashboard.page.load_time_ms                       | Histogram
dashboard.panel.{activity|notifications|actions}.{success|error|empty} | Counter
dashboard.mark_all_read.{attempted|succeeded|failed} | Counter
dashboard.quick_action.{id}.clicked              | Counter
api.dashboard.latency_ms                          | Histogram
api.dashboard.error_rate                          | Gauge (per 1m)
api.dashboard.partial_failure_rate                | Counter
```

**Structured log lines:**
- Endpoint entry: `{event: "dashboard_fetch_start", member_id, workspace_id}`
- Per-panel result: `{event: "dashboard_panel_result", panel: "activity|notifications|actions", status: "ok|error", latency_ms}`
- Endpoint exit: `{event: "dashboard_fetch_complete", panels_ok: N, panels_failed: N, total_ms}`
- Mutation: `{event: "mark_all_read", status: "ok|error", notif_count, snapshot_time}`

Debuggability: With these logs, a bug reported 3 weeks post-ship is fully reconstructable (which panels succeeded, which failed, what the member did).

### Section 9: Deployment & Rollout Review

No DB migration. ✓
No backward-compat risk (new endpoint, existing pages unchanged during rollout). ✓
